title.narrative: IOM Migration, Business and Human Rights in Asia
IOM Migration, Business and Human Rights in Asia

description.narrative:
Det övergripande målet för programmet är att främja full respekt för migrantarbetares mänskliga- och arbetsrättsliga rättigheter inom värdekedjor i Asien och fokuserar på viktiga regionala korridorer för arbetskraftsmigration, inklusive både ursprungs- och destinationsländer.
I enlighet med FNs vägledande principer för företagande och mänskliga rättigheter verkar insatsen för att säkra staters skyldighet att skydda (protect) migrantarbetares rättigheter, den privata sektorns ansvar att respektera och säkra (respect) migrantarbetares rättigheter i sina värdekedjor och rekryteringsprocesser, samt möjligheten till effektiva rättsmedel och kompensation för migrantarbetare vars rättigheter kränkts.
Länder som berörs av insatsen är Kambodja, Indonesien, Malaysia, Nepal, Filippinerna, Thailand och Vietnam. En regional komponent som involverar relevanta ASEAN-organ ingår också.

The overall objective of the programme is to promote full respect for the human and labour rights of migrant workers within supply chains in Asia. The contribution focuses on key regional labour migration corridors in Asia, including both countries of origin and destination.
In accordance with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, the contribution works to secure the duty of states to protect the rights of migrant workers, the responsibility of the private sector to respect the rights of migrant workers in their value chains and recruitment processes, and the access to effective legal remedies and compensation for migrant workers whose rights have been violated.
Countries included in the programme are Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Nepal, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam. A regional component involving relevant ASEAN bodies is also included.

The main objective of the contribution is to promote full respect for the human and labour rights of migrant workers within supply chains in Asia. A specific focus is given to women and migrants in situations of vulnerability. Central to the rationale of the MBHR Asia programme are the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and their "Protect, Respect and Remedy" framework and the programme outcomes are structured along this framework.
PROTECT (Outcome 1): Improved labour migration governance that holds private sector actors accountable in protecting migrant workers' rights from a multi-sectoral, rights-based and gender-responsive approach. Output 1.1 Increased capacities and technical resources of national and subnational authorities and regional bodies in Asia in the design and implementation of policies related to labour migration governance, Responsible Business Conduct and the protection of migrant workers' rights in coordination with the private sector and the Civil Society Organisations Output 1.2 Increased availability of rights-based, gender-responsive and inclusive support and information services for migrant workers in coordination with Civil Society organizations, migrant networks and service providers.
RESPECT (Outcome 2): Improved corporate due diligence practices of private sector entities that respect the rights of migrant workers across their entire supply chains and at all stages of labour migration. Output 2.1 Improved knowledge and tools of private sector entities in the implementation of human rights due diligence and ethical recruitment and employment standards. Output 2.2 Increased opportunities for private sector stakeholders to engage in dialogues and collective actions around the responsible and transparent management of labour migration processes and the development of industry-led advocacy initiatives.
REMEDY (Outcome 3): Enhanced access for migrant workers to effective and gender-sensitive state justice and corporate grievance and remediation mechanisms. Output 3.1 Improved knowledge and tools of state actors and the private sector in the implementation of grievance mechanisms and the effective remediation of rights violations and abuses experienced by migrant workers. Output 3.2 Increased capacities and resources of civil society, migrant-driven organizations and trade unions in advancing migrant workers´ access to state-based justice and corporate grievance mechanisms.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution IOM Migration, Business and Human Rights in Asia

description.narrative:
Some significant outputs and results in line with the work-plan and agreed objectives were achieved in 2024, which marked the first year of implementation of the programme: - The programme provided advocacy and technical assistance to governments that led to tangible policy improvements. For example, the 4th Philippine Human Rights Plan, launched in December 2024, now includes a dedicated chapter on migrant workers and their families, reflecting a stronger national commitment to upholding migrant workers rights. The programme also enhanced institutional capacities through multi-stakeholder dialogues and targeted capacity building initiatives. IOM convened multi-stakeholder dialogues and consultations at the national level in Cambodia, Nepal, the Philippines, Thailand and Viet Nam, enhancing collaboration among 204 stakeholders, including government entities, UN agencies, civil society organizations (CSOs), and the private sector. These engagements led to improved policy coherence and collective action in addressing challenges related to migration, business, and human rights.
- Additionally, IOM trained 349 government representatives (213 men, 136 women), including 226 local and 123 central authorities from Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Nepal and the Philippines on implementing policies to protect migrant workers. Training covered critical topics such as safe migration, ethical recruitment, regular migration pathways, and the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs). Most trainings incorporated gender sessions, equipping government officials with the knowledge and skills necessary to develop and implement gender sensitive policies that better safeguard migrant workers. At the community level, IOM's awareness raising events engaged 6,774 people (1,486 men, 2,533 women, 2,755 gender data not available), of which 4,419 were inperson and 2,355 were online, equipping migrant workers and their families with essential knowledge on safe migration. These efforts empowered communities to make wel-linformed migration decisions and advocate for improved gender-responsive services and protections to migrant populations.
- IOM launched 11 new partnerships with private companies, including global partnerships with IKEA, Panasonic and VF Corporation, resulting in private sector investment of USD 770,000 to support the MBHR Asia Theory of Change and programme objectives. Key achievements include the adoption of corporate migrant policies aligned with international standards on human and labour rights, strengthened capacity of the private sector to implement ethical recruitment and responsible employment, and the integration of migrant workers in human rights due diligence and remediation strategies. Notably, a corrective action plan developed by a supplier within an American multinational corporation's food and pet food supply chain in Thailand is expected to benefit 6,320 migrant workers (2,056 men and 4,264 women) who are employed by this supplier.
- IOM also delivered capacity building trainings, policy advisory and human rights due diligence (HRDD) assessments to 168 private sector entities. Notably, 16 were small and medium enterprises (SMEs)s, underscoring IOMs strengthened engagement with SMEs as critical actors in global supply chains. Gender and climate change were mainstreamed throughout implementation, including in assessment tools, dedicated training sessions and recommendations. As a highlight of 2024, IOM developed the first ever global human rights policy for a Swiss company, embedding gender-responsive ethical recruitment policies that promote greater gender equity in their supply chains.
- In line with the ambition to engage more with industry wide coalitions for broader impact, IOM launched two sector wide initiatives in Thailand, funded by AIM Progress and Bonsucro, to build capacities of suppliers in the sugar and fast moving consumer goods sectors, on migrant worker vulnerabilities and labour migration management systems.
- To enhance access to state justice and corporate grievance and remediation mechanisms, the MBHR Asia programme contributed to the revision of IOM's Operational Guidelines for Businesses on Remediation of Migrant Worker Grievances (originally developed under CREST Project), demonstrating the programmes ability to scale good practice globally. The updated global resource, which will be launched in 2025, strengthens practical guidance to businesses on engaging with migrant workers, including vulnerable groups such as women, children and persons with diverse SOGIESC. Importantly, an internal guidance on Access to Justice Fund was developed to set parameters and instructions for the implementing missions preparing MBHR Asia programme to be rolled out in 2025.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
